transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent mutable `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered the unsupported Rust slice pattern `if let [init @ .., last] = self` to the mechanically equivalent nonempty branch `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at_mut(slice.len() - 1)`, and `&mut tail[0]`; this preserves the init-prefix/last-element mutable data flow of the Rust body while using Verus-supported syntax.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions before taking the returned mutable last-element borrow, connecting the desugared init/tail views to the generated `old(slice)@[old(slice)@.len() - 1]`, prefix subrange, and final reconstruction contract without changing executable control flow or data flow.
